questions.question: Find the HCF of 24, 36 and 102.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

HCF is always a factor of the smallest difference between any two numbers.

Smallest difference between numbers: 36 − 24 = 12.

Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12.

Check the highest factor from the options that divides 102.

12 does not divide 102, but 6 divides 102 (102 ÷ 6 = 17).

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given values: 24, 36, 102

Formula used: HCF = Product of the lowest powers of common prime factors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e74f590998aa1728e21464847a96e09f42770eb1441cebee8a78253585822c14.png] 

⇒ Prime factors of 24 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 2³ × 3¹

⇒ Prime factors of 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 2² × 3²

⇒ Prime factors of 102 = 2 × 3 × 17 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 17¹

⇒ Common prime factors = 2¹ and 3¹

⇒ HCF = 2 × 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving any remainder is called their HCF or GCD (Greatest Common Divisor).

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. For example, 8 and 15 are co-prime.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of Fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

questions.question: Train A is 260 m long and crosses a platform of length 160 m in 28 seconds. Train B is 340 m long and passes a stationary man in 20 seconds. Both trains travel at constant speeds on parallel straight tracks. Find the time (in seconds) taken when the faster train completely overtakes the slower train while moving in the same direction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of A = (260 + 160) ÷ 28 = 420 ÷ 28 = 15 m/s

Speed of B = 340 ÷ 20 = 17 m/s

Relative Speed (Same direction) = 17 − 15 = 2 m/s

Total distance for overtaking = 260 + 340 = 600 m

Required time = 600 ÷ 2 = 300 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of Train A = 260 m, Platform = 160 m, Time A = 28 s

Length of Train B = 340 m, Time B (stationary man) = 20 s

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Relative Speed (Same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time to overtake = (Sum of Lengths) ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a6dd4b3ee0a21782e50ba1e9ed78b93098b1253a8f62aa753ada77e96871f22.png] 

⇒ Speed of Train A = (260 + 160) ÷ 28

⇒ Speed of Train A = 420 ÷ 28 = 15 m/s

⇒ Speed of Train B = 340 ÷ 20 = 17 m/s

⇒ Since Train B is faster (17 > 15), it will overtake Train A.

⇒ Relative Speed = 17 − 15 = 2 m/s

⇒ Total Distance to cover = 260 + 340 = 600 m

⇒ Time taken = 600 ÷ 2 = 300 s

**∴ The correct answer is 300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 

When moving in the same direction, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is S₁ + S₂.

Train Crossing Objects

To cross a point object (man/pole), distance = length of train. To cross a platform or another train, distance = sum of lengths.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: A rectangular piece of paper is 44 cm long and 89 cm wide. A cylinder is formed by rolling the paper along its length. Find the curved surface area of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a rectangular sheet is rolled to form a cylinder, the area of the sheet is always equal to the curved surface area (CSA) of the cylinder.

Area of Rectangular Paper = Length × Width

⇒ CSA of Cylinder = 44 × 89

⇒ CSA of Cylinder = 3916 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3916 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of paper (L) = 44 cm

Width of paper (W) = 89 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

Area of Rectangle = Length × Width

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae246df5ec953ed5b89a0ab04b587195a899d86a129f3734a615b33da886a0c9.png] 

When rolled along the length, the length becomes the circumference (2πr) and the width becomes the height (h).

⇒ Circumference (2πr) = 44 cm

⇒ Height (h) = 89 cm

⇒ Curved Surface Area (CSA) = (2πr) × h

⇒ CSA = 44 × 89

⇒ CSA = 3916 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3916 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r), which includes the curved area and the area of two circular bases.

Volume of Cylinder

The capacity or volume of a cylinder is calculated as V = πr²h.

Rolling Logic

If rolled along width, the width becomes the circumference (2πr = 89) and length becomes height (h = 44). The CSA remains unchanged.

questions.question: Which type of cell has very small vacuoles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Animal cell**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Animal cells** typically have **very small** and often **temporary vacuoles** compared to other eukaryotic cells like plants.
 
• In **Animal cells**, these vacuoles function in **storage**, **transport**, and the **secretion** of waste products or nutrients.
 
• **Plant cells** are distinguished by a single, **large central vacuole** that occupies most of the cell volume (up to 90%), providing **turgor pressure** and **structural support** to the plant.
 
• **Bacterial cells** are **prokaryotic** and generally lack **membrane-bound organelles**, meaning they do not possess true vacuoles like eukaryotic cells.
 
• **Fungal cells** contain vacuoles that are involved in **homeostasis**, **protein degradation**, and **storage**, and they are usually larger and more prominent than those found in animal cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The membrane that surrounds a vacuole is specifically called the **tonoplast**.
 
• The liquid content inside the plant vacuole is known as **cell sap**, which contains water, minerals, salts, and sugars.
 
• Certain **unicellular organisms** like **Amoeba** use **contractile vacuoles** for **osmoregulation**, which helps them pump out excess water to prevent the cell from bursting.
 
• **Food vacuoles** are formed in some animal-like protists and specialized animal cells through the process of **phagocytosis** to digest engulfed food particles.

questions.question:
What is the mode of the following data?

86, 84, 71, 82, 82, 63, 84, 71, 70, 86, 88, 65, 71, 81, 87, 60, 60, 74, 78, 62, 75, 66, 68, 85, 72
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set.

Count occurrences of the given numbers:

71 → 3 times | 86 → 2 times | 84 → 2 times | 82 → 2 times | 60 → 2 times

All other numbers appear only once.

Since 71 has the highest frequency (3), it is the mode.

**∴ The correct answer is 71.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given Data: 86, 84, 71, 82, 82, 63, 84, 71, 70, 86, 88, 65, 71, 81, 87, 60, 60, 74, 78, 62, 75, 66, 68, 85, 72

Formula Used: Mode = Value with the maximum frequency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cac687389d485bd68d539d3f3e1c5189090ec90ef90bf4461369b1e9a9c6ba6.png] 

⇒ Total items in data set = 25

⇒ Frequency (60) = 2

⇒ Frequency (71) = 3

⇒ Frequency (82) = 2

⇒ Frequency (84) = 2

⇒ Frequency (86) = 2

⇒ Frequency (other items) = 1

⇒ Highest frequency = 3, which belongs to 71.

**∴ The correct answer is 71.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

Relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Types of Mode

Data with one mode is Unimodal; with two modes is Bimodal; with more than two is Multimodal.

Median

The middle-most value when data is sorted. For N = 25, Median = (25+1)/2 = 13th term.

questions.question: If the frequency of a sound wave increases and the speed remains constant, its wavelength will:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decrease**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fundamental relationship between the **speed** of a sound wave, its **frequency**, and its **wavelength** is expressed by the wave equation: **Speed (v) = Frequency (f) × Wavelength (λ)**.
 
• According to this equation, **wavelength** can be calculated as **λ = v / f**.
 
• Since the **speed (v)** of the sound wave remains **constant**, the wavelength is **inversely proportional** to the frequency.
 
• When the **frequency (f) increases**, the denominator in the equation grows larger, which results in a **decrease** in the **wavelength (λ)** to keep the product constant.
 
• Conversely, if the frequency were to decrease while the speed remained the same, the wavelength would increase.
 
• Therefore, for a sound wave traveling at a fixed speed, a **higher pitch** (higher frequency) corresponds to a **shorter wavelength**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **speed of sound** is primarily determined by the **medium** through which it travels (solid, liquid, or gas) and its **temperature**. It does not depend on the frequency or amplitude of the wave itself.
 
• Sound travels fastest in **solids** (due to high elasticity and density) and slowest in **gases**.
 
• The **Standard Unit (SI)** for **frequency** is **Hertz (Hz)**, which represents cycles per second.
 
• The **audible range** of sound for humans is typically between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz**.
 
• **Ultrasound** refers to sound waves with frequencies higher than the upper limit of human hearing, while **Infrasound** refers to frequencies lower than the human hearing threshold.

BODMAS Rule

questions.question: Substances degraded easily by the biological processes are called as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Biodegradable**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Biodegradable** substances are materials that can be broken down or decomposed into simpler substances by the action of **microorganisms** such as bacteria, fungi, and earthworms.
 
• These substances are typically organic in nature and return to the soil as nutrients, thereby supporting the **biogeochemical cycles** of the ecosystem. Examples include **vegetable peels**, **paper**, **wood**, and **animal waste**.
 
• In contrast, **Non-biodegradable** substances are those that cannot be degraded by biological processes. They persist in the environment for a long time, often causing **pollution** and harm to wildlife. Examples include **plastics**, **glass**, and **heavy metals**.
 
• The terms **Hard material** and **Soft material** refer to the **physical properties** or mechanical strength of a substance (like resistance to scratching or deformation) and are irrelevant to the chemical or biological degradation of the material.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Decomposers** play a vital role in the environment by breaking down dead organic matter, preventing the accumulation of waste, and replenishing **soil fertility**.
 
• **Composting** is a controlled biological process that accelerates the decomposition of biodegradable materials to produce **humus**, which acts as an excellent organic fertilizer.
 
• The presence of **Non-biodegradable** waste in water bodies often leads to **Bioaccumulation** and **Biomagnification**, where toxic chemicals enter the food chain and increase in concentration at higher **trophic levels**.
 
• Modern environmental efforts focus on replacing non-biodegradable items with **Eco-friendly** alternatives like **Bioplastics**, which are designed to degrade faster under specific conditions.

questions.question: When an object is placed at infinity in front of a convex lens, the image formed is:

options.text: Virtual, inverted, and at the focus
Real, inverted, and at the focus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Real, inverted, and at the focus**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex lens** is also known as a **converging lens** because it bends parallel light rays inward toward a common point.
 
• When an object is placed at **infinity**, the incident light rays are considered to be **parallel** to the **principal axis**.
 
• According to the rules of **refraction** for spherical lenses, rays parallel to the principal axis pass through the **principal focus (F2)** on the other side of the lens after refraction.
 
• The resulting image has the following properties:
 
 
• **Position:** At the **focus (F2)**.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 50 mangoes at ₹10 each. He sold 30 mangoes at a profit of 20% and the remaining 20 mangoes at a loss of 10%. What is his overall profit or loss percentage?

questions.question: The colour of scattered light depends on the size of the scattering particles. Very fine particles scatter mainly which colour of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blue light**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **scattering of light** is the phenomenon in which light rays are deflected in various directions when they strike particles like **dust**, **water droplets**, or **gas molecules**.
 
• The color of the scattered light depends on the **size** of the scattering particles in the medium.
 
• **Very fine particles** (like air molecules) have dimensions smaller than the wavelength of visible light. These particles are highly effective at scattering light of **shorter wavelengths**.
 
• In the visible light spectrum, **blue light** has a shorter wavelength compared to red light. Therefore, fine particles in the atmosphere scatter the blue end of the spectrum more intensely.
 
• **Large particles**, such as raindrops or large dust particles, scatter all wavelengths of light almost equally. This is why **clouds** or **fog** usually appear **white**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rayleigh Scattering:** This law states that the intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of its wavelength ( I propto 1/lambda⁴ ). This explains why the **sky appears blue** during a clear day.
 
• **Red Light:** Red light has the **longest wavelength** in the visible spectrum (approximately 1.8 times that of blue light). Because it is scattered the least by fine particles, it is used for **danger signals** as it can be seen from long distances even through fog or smoke.
 
• **Sunrise and Sunset:** During these times, sunlight travels through a **thicker layer** of the atmosphere. Most of the shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) are scattered away, leaving only the **longer wavelengths (red/orange)** to reach the observer's eye.
 
• **Tyndall Effect:** This is the scattering of a beam of light by **colloidal particles** or a very fine suspension, which makes the path of the light beam visible.

questions.question: Two taps, A and B, can fill a cistern in 6 hours and 7.5 hours, respectively. Both the taps are opened for 2 hours and then B is turned off. How much time will A take to fill the remaining cistern?

Divide goods into three parts based on percentages: 55%, 9% (20% of 45%), and 36% (balance).

Apply weighted average: x = (55 × 41 + 9 × 19 − 36 × 21) ÷ 100

x = (2255 + 171 − 756) ÷ 100

x = 1670 ÷ 100 = 16.7%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Part 1 = 55% of goods at 41% profit.

Remaining goods = 100% − 55% = 45%.

Part 2 = 20% of 45% = 9% of goods at 19% profit.

Part 3 (Rest) = 45% − 9% = 36% of goods at 21% loss.

**Formula:**

Overall Profit/Loss % = [Σ (Quantity × Profit/Loss %)] ÷ Total Quantity

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09cc64c460c4be07fc6a04b31a7f5c2531e93ebd0b09c0b73333ded55671a6ab.png]

⇒ Profit from Part 2 = 9 × (19/100) = 1.71

⇒ Loss from Part 3 = 36 × (−21/100) = −7.56

⇒ Net Profit = 22.55 + 1.71 − 7.56 = 16.70

⇒ Overall Profit % (x) = (16.70 ÷ 100) × 100 = 16.7%

**∴ The correct answer is 16.7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question:
In this question, a question is followed by two statements numbered (I) and (II). You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question. Read both the statements and decide the appropriate answer.

Among the five poles—R, A, M, E, and N—each having a different height, which one is the shortest?

(I) E is taller than only one pole. R is taller than A.

(II) E is taller than N.

options.text: Both statements I and II together (and not statement I alone or statement II alone) are sufficient to answer the question
Both statements I and II together are NOT sufficient to answer the question
Data in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement I is not
Data in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question while data in statement II is not

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. E is taller than only one pole. R > A

II. E > N

Question: Who is the shortest pole among R, A, M, E, and N?

Analysis:

From Statement I:

E is taller than only one pole → E is 2nd shortest.

R > A gives only a partial comparison between R and A, but no information about M and N.

So Statement I alone is not sufficient.

From Statement II:

E > N

This only tells that N is shorter than E, but nothing about R, A, or M.

So Statement II alone is not sufficient.

Combining I and II:

E is taller than only one pole → exactly one pole is below E

From II, N is below E

So, the only pole below E must be N, making N the shortest pole.

Thus, combining both statements allows us to uniquely identify the shortest pole as N.

Hence, both statements I and II together are sufficient, but neither statement alone is sufficient.

Hence, the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

questions.question: What is the product when ethanol reacts with sodium?

options.text: Sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas evolve during the reaction with ethanol.
Sodium oxide and water evolve during the reaction with ethanol only.
Sodium carbonate and hydrogen gas evolve during the reaction with ethanol.
Sodium hydroxide and oxygen gas evolve during the reaction with ethanol.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas evolve during the reaction with ethanol.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **Ethanol** (ethyl alcohol) reacts with **Sodium** metal, it results in the formation of **Sodium ethoxide** and the evolution of **Hydrogen gas**.
 
• The reaction can be represented by the following chemical equation: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na rightarrow 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂ uparrow 
 
• In this reaction, sodium acts as a strong reducing agent and displaces the **acidic hydrogen** from the **hydroxyl group** (-OH) of the ethanol molecule.
 
• The evolution of **Hydrogen gas** is typically confirmed by the **Pop sound test**, where a burning splinter is extinguished with a characteristic 'pop' sound.
 
• **Sodium ethoxide** (C₂H₅ONa) is an **alkoxide**, which is the conjugate base of ethanol and is used extensively as a strong base in organic synthesis.
 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• **Sodium oxide** and **water** are not products of this metal-alcohol displacement reaction.
 
• **Sodium carbonate** requires a source of carbon and oxygen (like carbon dioxide), which is not part of this reaction pathway.
 
• **Oxygen gas** is not evolved; rather, it is the hydrogen from the alcohol group that is released.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Alcohols are generally **very weak acids**, even weaker than water, which is why they react with highly reactive **alkali metals** like sodium but do not typically react with weaker bases like sodium hydroxide.
 
• The reaction of sodium with ethanol is **less vigorous** compared to the reaction of sodium with water, making it a safer way to dispose of small scraps of sodium in a laboratory setting.
 
• This specific reaction is often used as a **confirmatory test** for the presence of the **Alcoholic functional group** in an organic sample.
 
• **Ethanol** is a primary alcohol and is the main constituent of alcoholic beverages, but in the lab, it is used as a solvent and chemical intermediate.

questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution ____________.

options.text: Are not enforceable by any court

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Are not enforceable by any court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)** are enumerated in **Part IV** of the **Constitution of India**. According to **Article 37**, these principles are **not enforceable by any court**, meaning they are **non-justiciable** in nature. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.*
 
• While they are not legally enforceable, the **Constitution** declares that these principles are **fundamental in the governance** of the country, and it shall be the duty of the **State** to apply these principles in making laws.
 
• Unlike **Fundamental Rights**, which can be enforced through **Article 32** or **Article 226** if violated, a citizen cannot move to the **Supreme Court** or **High Courts** for the implementation of **DPSPs**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• The **Supreme Court** has ruled in several cases, such as the **Minerva Mills Case (1980)**, that there must be a **harmonious construction** between **Fundamental Rights** and **Directive Principles**. Generally, **Directive Principles** do not override **Fundamental Rights**, except in very specific circumstances (like **Article 31C**). *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*
 
• Courts can, however, look into **DPSPs** while interpreting the validity of a law or the **Constitution**, but they cannot compel the government to enact a specific policy based on them. *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Origin and Scope:**

 
 
• The concept of **DPSP** was borrowed from the **Irish Constitution of 1937**, which had copied it from the **Spanish Constitution**.
 
• They span from **Article 36 to Article 51** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• These principles aim at establishing **social and economic democracy** in the country and envision a **Welfare State** rather than a mere police state.
 
 
 
• **Classification of DPSPs:**
 
 
• **Socialistic Principles:** These aim at providing social and economic justice. Examples include **Article 38** (promoting welfare), **Article 39** (equitable distribution of resources), and **Article 41** (right to work).
 
• **Gandhian Principles:** Based on the ideology of **Mahatma Gandhi**. Examples include **Article 40** (organization of **Village Panchayats**), **Article 43** (promotion of cottage industries), and **Article 47** (prohibition of intoxicating drinks).
 
• **Liberal-Intellectual Principles:** These reflect the ideology of liberalism. Examples include **Article 44** (**Uniform Civil Code**), **Article 50** (separation of judiciary from executive), and **Article 51** (promotion of international peace).
 
 
 
• **Significant Amendments:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** added four new **Directive Principles**: **Article 39** (opportunities for healthy development of children), **Article 39A** (equal justice and free legal aid), **Article 43A** (participation of workers in management), and **Article 48A** (protection of environment).
 
• The **86th Amendment Act of 2002** changed the subject matter of **Article 45** and made elementary education a **Fundamental Right** under **Article 21A**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar** described the **Directive Principles** as **"Novel Features"** of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• **Granville Austin** described the **Fundamental Rights** and the **Directive Principles** together as the **"Conscience of the Constitution"**.
 
• In the **Champakam Dorairajan case (1951)**, the **Supreme Court** ruled that in case of any conflict between **Fundamental Rights** and **DPSP**, the former would prevail. However, this was later refined in the **Minerva Mills Case** to emphasize a **balance** between the two.

questions.question: When a drop of ink is placed in water, it spreads evenly without stirring. What does this demonstrate?

options.text: Particles of matter are constantly moving
Particles are heavy and settle down

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Particles of matter are constantly moving**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon where ink spreads in water without any external force (like stirring) is known as **Diffusion**.
 
• **Diffusion** is the process of **spontaneous intermixing** of particles of two different types of matter on their own.
 
• This happens because the **particles of matter** are in a state of **continuous random motion**. This property is a fundamental characteristic of matter.
 
• The particles possess **Kinetic Energy**, which enables them to move and occupy the **intermolecular spaces** between the particles of the other substance (water in this case).
 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because if particles were at rest, the ink would remain concentrated at a single spot.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect because while a reaction might occur in some chemical systems, the physical spreading is primarily due to motion, not necessarily a chemical reaction.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because if particles were simply heavy and settled down, they would accumulate at the bottom of the container (sedimentation) rather than spreading **evenly** throughout the liquid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **rate of diffusion** increases with an increase in **Temperature**. This is because, with higher temperatures, the **kinetic energy** of the particles increases, causing them to move faster.
 
• Diffusion occurs most rapidly in **Gases**, slower in **Liquids**, and is slowest (almost negligible) in **Solids** due to the difference in the space between particles and their **force of attraction**.
 
• The concept of the random motion of particles in a fluid is also related to **Brownian Motion**, which provides further evidence that particles are constantly moving.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also known as the **cell membrane**, is a thin, delicate, and **flexible** boundary. It is **not rigid**; instead, it has a fluid-like consistency.
 
• **Rigidity** is a primary characteristic of the **cell wall**, which is a tough, non-living outer layer found in **plants**, **fungi**, and **bacteria** to provide structural support.
 
• The plasma membrane is the **outermost covering** of the cell (specifically in animal cells) that separates the internal contents from the external environment.
 
• It is **selectively permeable**, meaning it regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell, allowing only specific molecules to pass through while blocking others.
 
• The membrane is primarily composed of **lipids** (organized in a bilayer) and **proteins**, with small amounts of **carbohydrates** attached to them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The most widely accepted structure of the plasma membrane is the **Fluid Mosaic Model**, proposed by **S.J. Singer** and **G.L. Nicolson** in **1972**.
 
• The **fluidity** of the membrane is crucial for various biological processes such as **endocytosis** (engulfing food and other materials), **cell growth**, and **secretion**.
 
• In the phospholipid bilayer, the **hydrophilic heads** face outward toward the aqueous environment, while the **hydrophobic tails** face inward, away from water.
 
• **Proteins** in the membrane can be **peripheral** (on the surface) or **integral** (spanning across the membrane), serving as transporters or receptors.

questions.question: Which organisation hosted the National Agro-RE Summit 2025?

options.text: National Solar Energy Federation of India

questions.solution:
p data-end="57" data-start="0">The correct answer is __**National Solar Energy Federation of India**__.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Agro-RE Summit 2025** was hosted by the **National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI)** to foster collaboration between the agriculture and renewable energy sectors.
 
• The primary objective of the summit was to promote **Agrivoltaics**, a concept that combines **solar energy generation** with **agricultural production** on the same land.
 
• The event focused on the implementation of **Decentralized Renewable Energy (DRE)** solutions to enhance rural livelihoods and ensure energy security for farmers. ***Hence, the statement regarding NSEFI as the host is correct.***
 
• The summit provided a platform for **policymakers**, **industry leaders**, and **researchers** to discuss the integration of solar power in farming practices to achieve **India's net-zero targets**.
 
• It highlighted the importance of technological innovation in **solar pump systems** and **grid-connected solar plants** specifically designed for the Indian agricultural landscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI):**

 
 
• **NSEFI** is an umbrella organization representing the entire solar energy ecosystem in India. It was founded in **2013** to provide a common platform for solar developers, manufacturers, and stakeholders.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it works closely with the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** to advocate for policies that accelerate solar adoption across the country.
 
 
 
• **Agrivoltaics in India:**
 
 
• **Agrivoltaics** allows for the **dual use of land**, where solar panels are installed at a height that permits **crop cultivation** underneath, reducing land-use conflict.
 
• This method helps in **water conservation** as the shade from panels reduces soil moisture evaporation, and the panels themselves stay cooler due to transpiration from crops, increasing **energy efficiency**.
 
• India aims to reach a non-fossil fuel capacity of **500 GW** by the year **2030**, and integrating solar into agriculture is seen as a vital step towards this goal.
 
 
 
• **PM-KUSUM Scheme:**
 
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM)** was launched in **2019** to provide energy security to **farmers**.
 
• It consists of three components aimed at installing **solar pumps**, solarizing existing pumps, and setting up **small solar power plants** on barren lands.
 
• The scheme plays a major role in the **decarbonization** of the agricultural sector and provides an additional source of income for rural households through the sale of surplus power.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Environmental Impact:**

 
 
• The integration of **renewable energy** in farming helps reduce the dependency on **diesel-powered pumps**, significantly lowering **greenhouse gas emissions** in the rural sector.
 
• The use of **micro-grids** in villages can provide reliable **24/7 power supply**, facilitating better post-harvest processing and cold storage facilities.
 
 
 
• **Economic Benefits for Farmers:**
 
 
• Through **Agro-RE** projects, farmers can transition from being mere consumers of energy to becoming **"Urjadatas"** (energy producers), ensuring a steady **revenue stream** regardless of crop cycles.
 
• Government subsidies and **financial incentives** are often provided to **Small and Marginal Farmers** to adopt these sustainable technologies.

The logic followed here is:

**Logic:** **(First Number × 2) + 1 = Second Number**

For, **49 → 99 **→

⇒ 49 × 2 = 98

⇒ 98 + 1 = 99

For, **73 → 147 →**

⇒ 73 × 2 = 146

⇒ 146 + 1 = 147

Now, applying the same pattern for 26:

26 → ?

⇒ 26 × 2 = 52

⇒ 52 + 1 = 53

Hence, the number related to 26 is 53.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 1.**
